To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adaptor proteins Grb10 and Shc differentially modulate v-Src induced Kv1.3 phosphorylation and biophysical properties by altering the physical complexes associated between the channel and Src kinase.
the adaptor proteins n-Shc and the Grb10 protein modulate the biophysical and phosphorylation properties of Kv1. 3 ion channel in a manner dependent on the presence of vSrc kinase.
adaptor molecules Grb10 and Shc modulate the biophysical and tyrosine phosphorylating effects of v-Src kinase on the Kv1.3 channel protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of Kv1. 3 ion channels by the adaptor proteins, Shc and Grb 10, in the presence of the tyrosine kinase v-Src.
the role of adaptor proteins in the regulation of ion channel function by tyrosine kinase signaling.
the regulation of Kv1. 3 ion channels in the olfactory system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adaptor protein Grb10 and the SHC family member n-Shc differentially modulate Src-induced Kv1. 3 channel phosphorylation and biophysical properties.
adaptor proteins differentially modulate Src-induced phosphorylation and biophysics of Kv channels.
adaptor proteins, nShc and Grb 10, differentially modulate tyrosine phosphoryla tion of Kv1. 3 and the associated channel biophysical properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adaptor proteins Grb10 and Shc differentially modulate Src-induced tyrosine phosphorylations of Kv1.4 and Kv1.3 channels, respectively, and the biophysical properties of these channels.
the adaptor proteins n-Shc and/or Grb10 can modulate the biophysics of Kv 1.3 by regulating the amount of tyrosine phosphorylations of Kv 1.3 in the presence and absence of v-Src kinase.
Grb10, n-Shc, and Src kinase form a signaling complex that modulates the biophysical and functional properties of Kv1.2 channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adaptor proteins differentially regulate Kv1.3 phosphorylation, biophysical properties, or both in the presence of a Src kinase.
Grb10, a protein that has been shown previously to interact directly with Kv1.2 and Kv1.5, is able to modulate Kv1.3 phosphorylation and function in the presence of the Src kinase.
adaptor proteins can regulate the phosphorylation state and the biophysical properties of Kv1.
